title: Fort Solis
provenance: Reported by udance4ever (highball-db#868, 2026-11-01), Apple M1, macOS 27.2, Highball 0.10.23, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, D3DMetal, rated 1 of 5 after 1 minutes: the loading screen hangs at launch and a helper seems to crash. The backtrace attached to the report is Civilization III's (highball-db#867), not this game's, the GOG copy. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#868 (2026-11-03), engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r29, whose D3DMetal is GPTK 4.0b2 per the Metal HUD: past the loading screen to a picture of Mars with a white rectangle in the middle, then a freeze without a crash about 30 seconds later. That run's log ends with Metal's assertion 'MTLTextureDescriptor has invalid pixelFormat (0)'. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#868 (2026-11-05), r29 with mfplat set to Disabled in winecfg: while loading, the game stops for 10 to 15 seconds, then comes back to a black screen with the title music. That run's log still ends with the same Metal assertion, so a video still reached D3DMetal through Media Foundation. The environment wasn't restarted before that launch because another program was still running. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#868 (2026-11-06), r29, D3DMetal, with mfplat disabled for the game's Shipping exe: in game, at about 20 fps with stutter, 30 fps with the graphics settings at Low. The next launch, with nothing changed, ended after 87 seconds with exit code 15 before the game loaded its NVIDIA Streamline plugins, which the first run did. Both logs have 'mfplat.dll (which is needed by mf.dll) not found', the expected trace of the override, and both runs started without restarting the environment because another program was still running. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#868 (2026-11-07): the exe that needs Media Foundation disabled is Sycamore-Win64-Shipping.exe in Sycamore\Binaries\Win64. On a Wine 11 engine (revision and mode not stated, no log) the game ran as an 8 fps slideshow. Back on Wine 10 r29 it ran at about 20 fps up to the point the player gets control, without crashing, and the failed second launch didn't happen again. udance4ever again on highball-db#868 (2026-11-07T17:36Z), the log of the 8 fps Wine 11 run: engine x64-crossover26.3-r30, D3DMetal (the D3DMetal 4 line), with Enable DLSS (MetalFX) on in that environment, which the Wine 10 runs didn't have. Media Foundation wasn't disabled in that environment (Wine's mfplat loads in Sycamore-Win64-Shipping.exe) and the log has no Metal error, so on r30 the video didn't freeze it. Nothing in the log explains the 8 fps.
notes: Gets in game in one report on an M1 with D3DMetal on engine r29 once Media Foundation is disabled for Sycamore-Win64-Shipping.exe, at about 20 fps, 30 at Low settings, not a good experience yet (highball-db#868). Without that a video freezes it after the loading screen. On a Wine 11 engine it ran at about 8 fps. An Unreal Engine 5 game on Direct3D 12.

knownIssues.symptom: Hangs on the loading screen at launch (M1, D3DMetal, Wine 10 r28)
knownIssues.fix: engine r29 got past it for the reporter (highball-db#868), who then hit the freeze below

knownIssues.symptom: On engine r29 a white rectangle shows over a picture of Mars after the loading screen, and the game freezes about 30 seconds later without crashing (M1, D3DMetal from GPTK 4.0b2)
knownIssues.cause: a video. The log ends with Metal's 'MTLTextureDescriptor has invalid pixelFormat (0)' assertion, the error The Last Caretaker hit when its menu video went through Windows Media Foundation into D3DMetal, and disabling Media Foundation for the game's exe gets past it
knownIssues.fix: disable Media Foundation for the game's Unreal exe, Sycamore-Win64-Shipping.exe in Sycamore\Binaries\Win64, not fortsolis.exe: in winecfg add that exe on the Applications tab, then on the Libraries tab add mfplat and set it to Disabled. That got the reporter in game (highball-db#868, 2026-11-06, credit udance4ever). Setting it on fortsolis.exe alone left a black screen with the title music. On the Wine 11 engine r30 the game got past the video without the override (highball-db#868, 2026-11-07), but ran at about 8 fps there

knownIssues.symptom: A launch right after a working one ended after about a minute and a half without reaching the game (M1, D3DMetal, Wine 10 r29)
knownIssues.fix: not known. It didn't happen again on a later launch (highball-db#868, 2026-11-07)

knownIssues.symptom: On the Wine 11 engine r30 with D3DMetal it runs as a slideshow at about 8 fps (M1)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. That environment had Enable DLSS (MetalFX) on, and the game keeps its graphics settings per environment, so the Low preset set in the Wine 10 one didn't apply there. Either may explain it, neither is checked (highball-db#868)
knownIssues.fix: none known. Wine 10 r29 with D3DMetal runs it at about 20 fps
